chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara

He said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the most meritorious of what the Sunnah prescribed regarding voluntary fasting, so he said: Three days in every month: Thursday in the beginning of the month, and Wednesday in the middle of the month, and Thursday in the end of the month. I said to him: Is this all that the Sunnah has prescribed regarding fasting? He said: Yes.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific days recommended for voluntary fasting in Shia tradition according to the Sunnah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the specific lunar schedule for the 'Ayyam al-Beed' (White Days) as the preferred voluntary fasts, reflecting the Prophet's tradition of fasting on the 13th, 14th, and 15th of each lunar month. Imam al-Sadiq’s confirmation that this constitutes the entirety of the Sunnah in this context underscores the significance of consistency in these three days over other sporadic voluntary fasts. This practice is deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a means of spiritual purification and following the Prophetic model of regular devotion.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the most meritorious of what the Sunnah flowed with regarding the voluntary from the Fasts’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three days during the month – the Thursday in the beginning of the month, and the Wednesday in the middle of the month, and the Thursday in the end of the month’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘This is the entirety of what the Sunnah has flowed with regarding the Fast?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following:

’’Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the best tradition in optional fasting. The Imam replied, ‘It is three days of fasting every month. It is the first Thursday, the Wednesday after the tenth day and the last Thursday of a month.’ I then asked, ‘Is that all of the tradition about fasting?’ He replied, ‘Yes, this is all about it.’”
